name: Reference soil Sweden 17
summary: A textbook Podzol under boreal forest. Acids from the needle litter have stripped iron and organic matter from a bleached, ash-grey layer and redeposited them as a dark, rusty band below. Wetness lower down adds grey, gleyed patches.

info.Vegetation: Northern coniferous forest (pine, fir, birch) with blueberry and mosses

credit: Photo: ISRIC World Soil Reference Collection, CC BY-SA 3.0 https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ISRIC_monolith_SE-017.jpg — Site and horizon data condensed from ISRIC – World Soil Information https://isis.isric.org/monoliths/reference-soil-se017 — Feature notes written for this site.

horizons.name: O
horizons.description: Organic horizon of needles and partly decomposed plant remains; gradual smooth boundary.

horizons.name: E
horizons.description: Light gray (10YR 7/1 dry) loamy sand; moderate platy structure; albic (bleached) horizon; gradual boundary.

horizons.name: Bhs1
horizons.description: Loamy sand; moderate platy structure; illuvial accumulation of humus and Fe–Al sesquioxides; gradual boundary.

horizons.name: Bhs2
horizons.description: Very dark gray (7.5YR 3/1 dry) loamy sand; moderate platy structure; weakly cemented; humus and sesquioxide accumulation; gradual boundary.

horizons.name: Bgs
horizons.description: Light gray (2.5Y 7/2 dry) sandy clay; weak platy to massive structure; Fe accumulation with gray reduced zones (gleyic properties).

features.title: Needle litter and roots
features.description: Acidic coniferous litter. As it decomposes it releases organic acids that drive podzolization.

features.title: Abrupt O/E boundary
features.description: Sharp contact between the dark organic layer and the bleached mineral soil, typical of Podzols with little mixing by soil fauna.

features.title: Bleached quartz sand
features.description: Coatings of iron oxide and humus have been stripped from the sand grains, leaving their natural light grey color.

features.title: Humus–iron band
features.description: The dark Bhs band where organic-metal complexes washed down from above precipitate. This is the spodic horizon that defines a Podzol.

features.title: Iron accumulation
features.description: Rusty orange iron oxides precipitated in the lower B horizon.

features.title: Grey reduced patch (redox depletion)
features.description: Grey zone where iron was reduced and removed during periods of saturation. These are the gleyic properties in Gleyic Podzol.

features.title: Rounded gravel
features.description: Rounded stones from the glacial till parent material.

features.title: Platy structure
features.description: Horizontal plates in the compact, weakly cemented subsoil, which slow downward water movement.
